Hi Kimberly / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited to move to implementation. Before we lock in dates, the engineering leads asked for a focused plan on cost/perf tuning during onboarding. Our main concerns: predictable latency for live scoring, keeping token costs within our projection, and a safe quantization path that preserves accuracy on short financial prompts.

Can we cover these items in the first implementation sprint? Rough asks from our side:
- batching approach for bursty traffic (mobile app + nightly batch jobs)
- KV / prefix caching strategy for repeated prompts
- recommended quantization profile(s) for our model family (we use an open decoder with ~7B params)
- routing policy options for fallback/auto-scale (region-aware + cost gates)

I attached a small sample of our sequence-length distribution and a short CSV of typical payloads.

Looking for a 30–45m call this week to align on owners and milestones.

Thanks,
Alejandra Ruiz
Head of ML Infrastructure, FinRise
alejandra@finrise.com

Thanks — I can take the quant/bench work. A few quick notes after scanning the CSV:
- seq distribution: 75% of requests <= 64 tokens, 20% 65–256, 5% >256. This favors shorter-prefix caching and small-batch optimizations.
- concurrency: looks like typical p95 concurrency of ~12 for peak (mobile bursts) with nightly batch jobs that hit higher throughput (x3).

Initial technical approach (experiments we suggest during Sprint 0):
A) Baseline runs: fp16 on our tuned kernels to get latency / TCO baseline.
B) Int8 quant trials (GPTQ-style) on a few representative checkpoints — measure top-1 logits drift on your eval set. If drift < 0.6% and perplexity delta acceptable, we can recommend int8-prod profile for batch flows.
C) Hybrid routing: prefer int8 for nightly bulk scoring, fp16 (or afp16) for low-latency interactive flows.
D) KV prefetch: enable prefix caching for the 75% short requests; set TTL to 30s and capacity per host tuned to p99 working set.

I'll prepare a small runbook and the scripts we'll use to produce the bench table on Friday.

- Monica Patel
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in routing/ops details. A few operational constraints and our recommended rollout cadence: 
1) Canary policy: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% (24–48h observation windows) with automatic rollback on error spike or latency SLO breach.
2) Routing policy: region-aware primary (us-west) with cost-tier fallback (int8-cost-tier) and a cold backup in us-east. We can expose a per-route config you can toggle from the Console for early-stage experiments.
3) Autoscale guardrails: keep max-batch-size capped for p99 latency protection; we’ll recommend a batch cap of 8 for interactive and 64 for batch jobs initially.
4) Logging & alerts: token-level cost reports and a latency tracer will be enabled for the canary.

I can join the alignment call Thu 3pm PT and will bring the canary DAG and rollout template.

- Karthik Iyer
Platform & Routing Lead, Redwood Inference
